event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: UPS’s 2024 Form 10-K offers only a brief, catch-all reference to “epidemics, pandemics” as one of several disruptive disaster scenarios. The company neither names COVID-19 nor quantifies specific impacts such as supply-chain bottlenecks, labor shortages, or changes in delivery patterns that were widely reported during 2020-2022. Instead, the wording is general and forward-looking: pandemics ‘have in the past and may in the future disrupt our business.’ Because the disclosure acknowledges historical disruption, it recognizes that COVID-19 (and possible future outbreaks) is more than a purely hypothetical threat, yet the lack of detail signals that management believes the acute phase has passed. Given the filing date (Feb 2024) is roughly four years after the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic, Time Decay dictates a mid-range risk score. Overall, the evidence reflects a moderate, unquantified, still-relevant risk that is now largely embedded within broader disaster planning, rather than a pressing, high-severity issue.

evidence_list.snippet: Weather conditions or other natural or man-made disasters and the increased severity or frequency thereof (including as a result of climate change), including storms, floods, fires, earthquakes, rising temperatures, epidemics, pandemics, conflicts, civil or political unrest, or terrorist attacks, have in the past and may in the future disrupt our business.

components.reason: Explicitly lists ‘epidemics, pandemics’ as potential disruptors to the business.
States that such events ‘have in the past’ disrupted operations, indicating historical (COVID-19) impact.
Also flags future disruption as possible (‘may in the future’), showing ongoing relevance.
Highly generic; no COVID-19 name, no quantitative or operational specifics provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: The sentence acknowledges past and potential future pandemic disruption but remains generic and unquantified. Per Time Decay (event ~4 years old), the resulting 4/10 score reflects a moderate, lingering risk.
